answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates from beacon nodes through random walks capped at a fixed length, limiting influence from distant identities. An attacker may forge many sybil identities, but if their cluster connects to honest nodes through a sparse external cut, its low conductance restricts walk flow across that boundary. Given bounded walk length and fixed trusted seed mass, min-cut transitivity bounds therefore limit the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, even in the mesa network.
